chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muawiya ibn 'Ammar, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'When a man enters into the Sa'ee (circumambulation) between As-Safa and Al-Marwa, and the time for prayer enters, should he slow down, or should he cut it off, pray, and return, or remain as he is in his state until he finishes?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Is there not a place of prostration (Masjid) upon both of these? No, but he should pray, then return.' I said: 'Should he sit upon both of these?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Or is he not like one who performs Sa'ee upon the animal?'

key_terms.السَّعْي: Sa'ee (ritual walking between Safa and Marwa)
key_terms.الْمَرْوَة: Al-Marwa (the second of the two hills)

ai.seo_question: What should a pilgrim do if prayer time enters while performing Sa'ee between Safa and Marwa?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the pilgrim should pause the Sa'ee to perform the obligatory prayer and then resume, rejecting the notion of continuing the ritual while standing or sitting in a manner that neglects the prayer's dignity. The Imam’s rhetorical question regarding 'riding beasts' highlights that the physical location of Safa and Marwa is not inherently a fixed prayer niche (mihrab) that suspends the duty of Salah, emphasizing the balance between ritual continuity and timely worship. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential principle that specific acts of worship do not override the fixed times of the five daily prayers, even during Hajj rituals.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Muawiya Bin Ammar who said,

‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘The man enters into the Sa’ee between Al-Safa and Al-Marwa, so the time for the Prayer comes up, should he slow down, or should he cut it off and he should Pray and return, or stay affirmed just as he is upon his state until he is free?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Or is there not a place of Prostration (Masjid) upon both of these? No, but he should Pray, then he should return’. I said, ‘He can sit upon both of these?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Or is he not like that performing Sa’ee upon the animal?’
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Mu‘awiyah ibn ‘Ammar who has said the following:

“I once asked abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a man who begins Sa‘y between al-Safa’ and al-Marwah but it becomes the time for Salat (prayer); if he can slow down, or stop and perform Salat (prayer), then return or remain standing until it is free. He (the Imam) said, ‘Is there no there Masjid on them? No, he must perform Salat (prayer) then return? I then asked, ‘Can he sit down on them?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘Is it not the case that he performs Sa‘y between al-Safa’ and al-Marwah while riding on animals?’
